summary: Empirically, OpenRouter upstream backends serving the SAME model id differ substantially in tool-calling correctness. Replaying one real captured agent payload (11 messages, 24 tools, reasoning=medium) 12 times per backend against qwen/qwen3.6-27b: Alibaba 12/12 clean, CoreWeave 12/12 clean, Morph 12/12 clean, Chutes 1/12 leaked, Phala 1/12 leaked, SiliconFlow 3/12 leaked. Two open questions this session could not close. (1) Mechanism: quantization does NOT explain it -- CoreWeave is fp8 and clean while Phala is unquantized and leaks -- so the cause is backend-specific template extraction, unconfirmed. (2) Durability: backend rosters and behavior change over time, so the shipped allowlist in scripts/goose-openrouter-route-proxy.py (DEFAULT_ONLY) is a dated snapshot, not a stable fact. Note also that 0/12 leaves a ~22 percent 95-percent upper bound on the true leak rate per backend (~10 percent pooled) -- 'clean' here means 'not observed to leak', not 'proven safe'.
proposed_touch_points: scripts/goose-openrouter-route-proxy.py (DEFAULT_ONLY) -- needs a re-measurement cadence rather than a hardcoded list; consider a `--measure` mode that replays a captured payload N times per backend and reports leak rates, so the allowlist can be regenerated from evidence instead of hand-edited, and so users on other models can derive their own
resolved_evidence: Closed by design 2026-07-31: upstream-backend tool-calling variance is provider-side. The same OpenRouter model id served by different upstreams differs in fidelity (Alibaba 12/12 and CoreWeave 12/12 clean, Morph degraded); nothing in agentteams/ can change a third party's backend. The measurement is retained in this row's summary as the reason, per the plan at tmp/by-week/2026-W31/cluster-plans-round-2.plan.md.

summary: agentteams/research/search.py::web_search could not distinguish 'the search endpoint blocked us' from 'nothing matched' -- both returned []. Root cause: DuckDuckGo answers a challenged request with HTTP 202 plus an interstitial anomaly/challenge page rather than an error status, so resp.raise_for_status() never fires (202 IS a success code); the challenge page simply yields no regex matches. Measured deterministic 2026-07-24: a long specific query returned 202 with zero results on 4/4 attempts while a shortened form of the same query returned 200 with 10 results. Observed live: an agent that had correctly adopted the tool received [] and was on track to conclude the information did not exist. Fixed by adding _broaden + web_search_verbose (retry once with a broadened query; return a note explaining the fallback or the block) with the CLI printing the note to stderr so stdout JSON stays parseable.
proposed_touch_points: agentteams/research/search.py -- the broadening heuristic (keep the first 4 terms) is a single fixed strategy chosen from one day's observations; consider measuring challenge behavior across query shapes before treating it as general, and consider whether other endpoints (or a fallback engine) should back it up. Also worth auditing other callers of web_search (reputable.py, news.py) that still consume the plain list and therefore cannot see the note
resolved_evidence: _DDG_CHALLENGE_STATUS discrimination plus web_search_verbose's note; tests/test_research_search.py.

summary: Partial fence adoption duplicates sections, and this repo's own .claude/ team has accumulated 40 pending collisions across 19 files. When a template fences a section a deployed team predates, --update --merge ADDS the fenced block while the deployed file's unfenced copy of the same section is preserved unconditionally, leaving two copies of which one is stale. _is_whole_body_migration solved this for the case where the deployed file's only fence is the whole-body content wrap; the partial case has no equivalent. Measured 2026-08-01 by dry run against .claude/agents: 40 collisions, worst offenders quality-auditor.md and technical-validator.md at 5 each, and the single most-duplicated section is '## Invariant Core' at 12 — i.e. twelve agent files would carry two copies of their own 'do not modify or omit' contract, which fences.py's own docstring calls worse than not updating at all. None of this is caused by the 2026-08-01 fencing work; that work made it VISIBLE by adding _detect_duplicate_sections, which now reports each collision in both the dry-run and real-run paths. The backlog is the reason .claude/ was NOT regenerated at the close of that session: a regen is safe only once these are resolved.
proposed_touch_points: Resolve the 40 collisions before the next .claude/ regen — each needs a human look at whether the deployed unfenced copy carries project edits, which is exactly why fences._detect_duplicate_sections reports rather than auto-resolves (auto-replacing would repeat the out-of-fence destruction fixed in _is_whole_body_migration the same day). Consider a bounded helper that, for a collision where the unfenced copy is byte-identical to the fenced one modulo whitespace, deletes the unfenced copy automatically and leaves the rest for review — that subset is provably safe and is likely most of the 12 Invariant Core cases.
